answer: Each agent must post a bond locked in a public contract before it can earn reputation-weighted rewards; if it double-signs a task or fails a randomly audited claim, the bond is slashed. Auditors are selected from agents with bonds at risk, so inventing a knoll of disposable identities does not create free influence: every identity needs capital, and coordinated fraud risks losing it. A karst of linked wallets or a mesa of fresh accounts still faces the same per-agent bond, making the attack costly to scale.
